title: Module overview
body:
This module develops the operational and geometric foundations of curved spacetime. The equivalence principle, local free fall, tidal gravity, the metric and its inverse and volume structures, line elements, proper time, null curves, causal structure, local flatness, and signature conventions establish the framework used throughout GR.

Begin with what a falling observer measures, then distinguish local inertial behaviour from tidal differences across a region. The metric, its inverse and its volume measure turn that physical picture into rules for clocks, light signals and integration.
statement: Local free fall, metric measurement and tidal comparisons establish the geometric starting point for GR.

title: Module overview
body:
This module progresses from comparing vectors at neighbouring events to describing free motion and tidal separation. Connections, Christoffel symbols, covariant derivatives, compatibility and torsion, parallel transport, geodesics and their variational equation, four-velocity, four-acceleration, and geodesic deviation form one connected account.

The same comparison rule appears in covariant differentiation, parallel transport and the geodesic equation. Work from that shared idea before using the component formulas. Local calculations distinguish changing coordinate components from measured acceleration.
statement: Connections compare neighbouring tangent spaces; their transport rule leads to free motion and tidal deviation.

title: Module overview
body:
This module constructs the hierarchy from Riemann curvature through the Ricci, scalar, and Einstein tensors. The Bianchi identity and curvature invariants provide consistency and diagnostics, while the Einstein-Hilbert action bridges curvature scalars to gravitational dynamics.

Follow the information lost in successive contractions from Riemann to Ricci to scalar curvature. Keep geometric identities separate from physical field equations, and distinguish an interior variational calculation from a complete boundary-value problem.
statement: Curvature measures the failure of local comparisons to agree; its contractions and identities build the gravitational action.

title: Module overview
body: This module explains how matter sources geometry and how Einstein's equations are constrained and specialised. Stress-energy, fluid matter, energy conditions and conservation lead to the field equations, cosmological term, matter variation, and trace-reversed and vacuum forms.

title: Module overview
body: This module connects full general relativity to Newtonian gravity, classical observations, and weak radiation. Weak metric perturbations, Newtonian and post-Newtonian limits, gravitational redshift, light deflection, perihelion precession, and gravitational waves show how measurable corrections and propagating tidal effects emerge from the theory.

title: Module overview
body: This module develops the central exact vacuum geometry around a spherical mass. The Schwarzschild metric and radius lead to horizons, the distinction between coordinate and curvature singularities, and an effective-potential description of timelike and null orbits.
